name: St. Mary's Basilica
architect: Leonard Darscheid; R. A. Gray & George Gallagher
history: The parish was founded in 1881 with an adobe church, and was Phoenix's only parish until 1924. The present church was built from 1902 to 1914 and dedicated in 1915. Pope John Paul II named it a basilica in 1985 and visited it in 1987.
arch: Mission Revival and Spanish Colonial Revival, with twin bell towers topped by onion domes, a nod to the Bavarian and Austrian roots of the pastor and architectural consultant. Four domes span the length of the church.
features: It has Arizona's largest collection of stained glass windows.
A 26-rank Schantz pipe organ fills the nave.

look.d: The onion domes come from Bavaria and Austria, home of the pastor and his consultant.
The upper windows show the life of Mary; the lower ones honour Franciscan saints.

fun: The towers' four bells still ring daily over downtown Phoenix.
journal: Desert stucco wearing Bavarian onion domes. Phoenix's first parish, and it shows it off.

quiz.q: Until what year was it Phoenix's only parish?
